Not service by mail; not service by publication. removal_reason: Not available. Do NOT file a notice of removal. The client confirmed (reply to QUESTIONS.md, 2026-09-28) that Harbor Street Bakery LLC has exactly two members: Noor Haddad (65%, lives Portland, Oregon) and Caleb Sorensen (35%, lives Seattle (Ballard), Washington). Under Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006) and Carden v. Arkoma Associates, 494 U.S. 185 (1990), an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its members are citizens - so Harbor Street is a citizen of BOTH Washington and Oregon (never of Delaware, and its Portland principal place of business is irrelevant). Plaintiff Sound Cascade Foods, Inc. is a citizen of Washington (incorporated there, principal place of business Kent; 28 U.S.C. 1332(a), (c)(1)). A Washington citizen suing a Washington-citizen defendant destroys complete diversity: no 'citizens of different States' under 28 U.S.C. 1332(a), so the federal court would have no subject-matter jurisdiction. Independently, the forum-defendant rule of 28 U.S.C. 1441(b)(2) bars diversity removal because the action was brought in Washington and the only properly joined and served defendant, Harbor Street, is (through Sorensen) a citizen of Washington. The amount in controversy IS met ($129,156.40 pleaded; $110,916.40 on the contract alone, both over $75,000 exclusive of interest and fees) but that one element cannot support removal. The removal_deadline of 2026-10-13 is the computed outer limit of the 30-day period of 28 U.S.C. 1446(b)(1) (service/receipt 2026-09-11; day 30 Sun 10/11 rolled past federal Columbus Day 10/12) and is retained only as the computed record; it is moot because no notice may or will be filed. Had one been filed, 28 U.S.C. 1447(c) would require remand for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction at any time before final judgment and 'may require payment of just costs and any actual expenses, including attorney fees' - i.e., Harbor Street would pay Sound Cascade's fees for a jurisdictionally void filing. The if_removed block below is retained for schema completeness only; it is a MOOT hypothetical schedule (it assumed a notice filed 2026-09-30). Two flagged caveats do not change the conclusion: (1) the library states that an individual is a citizen of the state of his or her domicile, and Sorensen's intent to remain in Seattle is not documented (client has no further information) - but the removing party must affirmatively establish complete diversity, and the only reported fact places this member in the forum state, so no notice can be signed in good faith; (2) membership percentages and commencement-date membership rest on the client's statement; the operating agreement and cap table have not been produced.
rules_relied_on: Wash. Super. Ct. Civ. R. 12(a)(1) and 4(a)(2) - 20-day answer after service; 60-day extensions inapplicable to personal service on a registered agent (library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md)
Wash. Super. Ct. Civ. R. 6(a) - state computing-time rule; last day rolls only for Saturday, Sunday or RCW 1.16.050 legal holiday (library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md)
Wash. Super. Ct. Civ. R. 6(e) - 3-day mail extension applies to CR 5 papers, not to the CR 4 summons; not applicable here (library/wa_cr_4_6_12.md)
RCW 1.16.050 - Washington legal holidays for 2026; Washington does not observe Columbus Day, so state courts are open 2026-10-12 (library/rcw_1_16_050_wa_holidays.md)
Wash. Super. Ct. Civ. R. 55(a)(3) - a party who has appeared is entitled to 5 days' written notice of a default motion; an informal notice of appearance counts (library/wa_cr_55_default.md)
28 U.S.C. 1446(b)(1) - notice of removal within 30 days after receipt by the defendant, through service or otherwise, of a copy of the initial pleading (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)
28 U.S.C. 1446(c)(1) - as reproduced in the library, a case may not be removed under 1446(b)(3) on the basis of diversity more than 1 year after commencement (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)

28 U.S.C. 1332(a) and (c)(1) - $75,000 matter in controversy exclusive of interest and costs; corporation deemed citizen of state of incorporation and of principal place of business (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)

Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006); Carden v. Arkoma Associates, 494 U.S. 185 (1990) - an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its members are citizens; one non-diverse member destroys diversity (library/llc_citizenship_cases.md)
28 U.S.C. 1441(a) - removal to the district embracing the place where the action is pending (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)

28 U.S.C. 1441(b)(2) - forum-defendant rule: no diversity removal if any properly joined and served defendant is a citizen of the state where the action is brought (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)
28 U.S.C. 1447(c) - remand of procedural defects must be moved within 30 days; jurisdictional defects at any time; remand may carry costs and attorney fees (library/28usc_1332_1441_1446_1447.md)

Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1) and 6(a)(6) - federal computing-time rule; last day that is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday rolls to the next non-holiday day; Columbus Day is a federal legal holiday (library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md)
5 U.S.C. 6103 and W.D. Wash. general order - Clerk's Office closed Monday, 2026-10-12 (Columbus Day) (library/federal_holidays_2026.md)
Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(d) - 3-day extension runs only from Rule 5(b)(2)(C)/(D)/(F) service of papers, not from Rule 4 service of the summons; not applicable here (library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md)
Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(a)(1)(A) - federal answer otherwise 21 days after service, shown for contrast with the 20-day state rule (library/frcp_4_5_6_12_excerpts.md)

Fed. R. Civ. P. 81(c)(2) - after removal, a defendant who did not answer must answer within the longest of 21 days after receiving the initial pleading, 21 days after service of the summons, or 7 days after the notice of removal is filed (library/frcp_81c_removed_actions.md)
Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2) - scheduling order within the earlier of 90 days after any defendant has been served or 60 days after any defendant has appeared (library/frcp_16_26f.md)
Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(1) - parties must confer as soon as practicable and at least 21 days before the scheduling conference or the Rule 16(b) scheduling order date (library/frcp_16_26f.md)
